verses.1: And Saul was consenting to his death. And there arose on that day a great persecution against the church which was in Jerusalem, and they were all scattered abroad throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria, except the apostles.
verses.2: And devout men buried Stephen and made great lamentation over him.
verses.3: But Saul laid waste the church, entering into every house, and dragging men and women committed them to prison.
verses.4: They therefore that were scattered abroad went about preaching the word.
verses.5: And Philip went down to the city of Samaria and proclaimed to them the Christ.
verses.6: And the crowds gave heed with one accord to the things that were spoken by Philip, when they heard and saw the signs which he did.
verses.7: For from many who had unclean spirits, they came out, crying with a loud voice, and many who were paralyzed and lame were healed.
verses.8: And there was much joy in that city.
verses.9: But there was a certain man named Simon, who had previously practiced sorcery in the city and amazed the people of Samaria, claiming to be someone great.
verses.10: They all gave heed to him, from the least to the greatest, saying, "This man is the power of God that is called Great."
verses.11: And they gave heed to him because for a long time he had amazed them with his sorceries.
verses.12: But when they believed Philip as he preached good news about the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women.
verses.13: And Simon himself also believed, and after being baptized he continued with Philip. And seeing signs and great miracles performed, he was amazed.
verses.14: Now when the apostles at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent to them Peter and John,
verses.15: who came down and prayed for them that they might receive the Holy Spirit,
verses.16: for He had not yet fallen on any of them, but they had only been baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
verses.17: Then they laid their hands on them and they received the Holy Spirit.
verses.18: Now when Simon saw that the Holy Spirit was given through the laying on of the apostles' hands, he offered them money,
verses.19: saying, "Give me this power also, so that anyone on whom I lay my hands may receive the Holy Spirit."
verses.20: But Peter said to him, "May your silver perish with you, because you thought you could obtain the gift of God with money!
verses.21: You have neither part nor lot in this matter, for your heart is not right before God.
verses.22: Repent therefore of this wickedness of yours, and pray to the Lord that, if possible, the intent of your heart may be forgiven you.
verses.23: For I see that you are in the gall of bitterness and in the bond of iniquity."
verses.24: And Simon answered, "Pray for me to the Lord, that none of the things you have spoken may come upon me."
verses.25: Now when they had testified and spoken the word of the Lord, they returned to Jerusalem, preaching the gospel to many villages of the Samaritans.
verses.26: And an angel of the Lord said to Philip, "Rise and go toward the south to the road that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza." This is a desert road.
verses.27: And he rose and went. And behold, an Ethiopian man, a eunuch of great authority under Candace, queen of the Ethiopians, who was in charge of all her treasure, had come to Jerusalem to worship
verses.28: and was returning, sitting in his chariot, and was reading the prophet Isaiah.
verses.29: And the Spirit said to Philip, "Go over and join this chariot."
verses.30: So Philip ran to him and heard him reading Isaiah the prophet and asked, "Do you understand what you are reading?"
verses.31: And he said, "How can I, unless someone guides me?" And he invited Philip to come up and sit with him.
verses.32: Now the passage of Scripture he was reading was this: "He was led like a sheep to the slaughter, and as a lamb before its shearer is silent, so He does not open His mouth.
verses.33: In His humiliation His judgment was taken away. Who can describe His generation? For His life is taken from the earth."
verses.34: And the eunuch said to Philip, "I ask you, about whom does the prophet say this — about himself or about someone else?"
verses.35: And Philip opened his mouth, and beginning from this Scripture, preached Jesus to him.
verses.36: And as they were going along the road they came to some water, and the eunuch said, "Look, here is water! What is to prevent me from being baptized?"
verses.37: And Philip said, "If you believe with all your heart, you may." And he answered and said, "I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God."
verses.38: And he commanded the chariot to stop, and they both went down into the water, both Philip and the eunuch, and he baptized him.
verses.39: And when they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord carried Philip away, and the eunuch saw him no more, for he went on his way rejoicing.
verses.40: But Philip was found at Azotus, and as he passed through he preached the gospel to all the cities until he came to Caesarea.
